title: Common strata carrying finite-type module trivializations
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $R$ a commutative ring, and choose either the small étale sites of all schemes or their small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the corresponding inverse-image restrictions [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $F_1,\ldots,F_r$ be a finite family of such module sheaves on $X$. Suppose for each $j$ there is an open covering of $X$ on each member $U$ of which a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] by constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] locally closed subschemes makes $F_j$ locally constant of finite type; this means locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf]. Then there is one open covering on each member $U$ of which there is a finite stratification $i_\lambda:T_\lambda\to U$ making all $F_j$ locally constant of finite type; this covering may be taken to consist of all intersections $U=U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_r$ with each $U_j$ a member of the $j$-th input covering. More precisely, after restricting the input stratification of each $U_j$ to $U$, one may take $T_\lambda$ to be the nonempty finite fibre products over $U$ of one stratum from each input stratification [def-pc-fibre-product]. These are constructible locally closed subschemes with pairwise disjoint images covering $U$ and have the actual projection morphisms $h_{\lambda,j}$ to the input strata. For every chosen local trivialization of an input restriction with model $M$, its covering pulls back to a covering of $T_\lambda$ on which $i_\lambda^*F_j$ is the constant module sheaf with the same model $M$. The identification uses the canonical constant-ring inverse-image isomorphism, adjoint to constant sections, and is compatible with the inverse-image composition isomorphism for $i_\lambda$ and $h_{\lambda,j}$. No finiteness of the underlying set of $R$ or Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is assumed. The empty family admits the one-stratum stratification $U=X$.

source.place: Tag 093R, lemma-pullback-locally-constant (including modules over a fixed ring); the finite fibre-product refinement and constant-section compatibility expand the common-strata argument in the retained finite-reductions proof Step 6.

proof.text: For each x in X choose one member of each of the finitely many input open coverings containing x. Their intersection contains x, proving the asserted intersection covering, including r=0.

For each intersection U apply the finite wide-pullback refinement theorem to the original strata over their opens. Keep its limiting cones, actual vertex identifications, projection to U, nonempty strata for r nonzero and singleton identity stratum for r=0. Define each projection to the original stratum from the corresponding limiting-cone leg. Its composite to X agrees with the common stratum map by the cone equations.

For the coefficient identifications, use the prescribed sheafification and module adjunctions directly. Base change on either scheme site preserves finite limits and hence the terminal object; AsSmall transport preserves this property. The composite of constant sheafification with ring inverse image and target constant sheafification are left adjoint to the same terminal evaluation functor. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an isomorphism, and its adjunct is rho because both fix constant scalars. For a module M, construct the normalized constant comparison by sheafifying the presheaf map sending m to the constant section m after base change, checking linearity using the scalar equation. Evaluation at a terminal object classifies maps from a constant module presheaf. Thus precomposition by the specified module comparison is bijective on maps into every module sheaf: the two module sheafification adjunctions and the inverse-image adjunction identify it with restriction of scalars along the same constant-section ring equation. The coyoneda criterion makes this comparison invertible, for arbitrary M and R. These are the completed Lean proofs of adicStratificationRingMap_isIso, adicStratificationConstantMap_existsUnique and adicStratificationConstantMap_isIso; no geometric algebraic-structure lift is needed for these canonical module pullbacks.

proof.text: Specify direct-image pasting on sections by restriction along the finite-fibre-product pasting isomorphism. The scalar maps agree by checking constant scalars under the ring sheafification adjunction. Mathlib pushforwardComp followed by pushforwardCongr₂ supplies this isomorphism, uniquely characterized by its section maps (adicStratificationPushforwardComp_existsUnique). Its adjunction mate is the specified inverse-image composition isomorphism. The conjugate adjunction unit identity computes the adjunct of composition through that mate. Applying the constant-module comparisons twice sends each generator m to m on the iterated fibre product. Naturality of the constant-module sheafification unit identifies this with the direct constant section under pasting. The uniqueness proved in the preceding step therefore gives adicStratificationConstantMap_comp. This completes the constant-section composition compatibility in Lean.

proof.text: Both scheme base-change site functors preserve finite limits, and so do AsSmall.up and AsSmall.down. Obtain finite limits on the small models and finite-limit preservation of model base change by transport. CoverPreserving.of_isContinuous gives functor-pushforward covering preservation. Use the existing normalized constant-module comparison isomorphisms for every module.

For each product projection h and original sheaf restriction G, the already specified adicStratificationProjectionComparison identifies the common restriction P with h*G. Apply finite_type_constant_module_pullback with this comparison, the constant comparison isomorphisms, and the input local-constancy hypothesis. This proves the locallyConstant field with unchanged finite module models.

Every chosen covering sieve pulls forward to a covering by CoverPreserving.of_isContinuous. For every chosen local isomorphism e with model M, apply normalized_local_module_pullback with c equal to the specified adicStratificationConstantMap isomorphism and b equal to adicStratificationProjectionComparison. Its exact unique unit-normalized equation is the required AdicStratificationTrivializationCompatibility. The compatibility predicate is definitionally the specialization of the shared NormalizedLocalModuleTrivialization predicate. Together these fields construct CommonRefinement; all existing declaration types and the quantified normalization equation are preserved.

tool_uses.why: The generic geometric base-change theorem constructs actual scheme strata, with their images, on arbitrary bases; it does not replace the integral-models route.
Generic constructible-subset inverse image under any scheme morphism; needed for restriction to arbitrary intersections of opens without Noetherian hypotheses.
Only clause (e), composition of immersions, is used to embed the iterated fibre-product strata.
Generic small-etale geometric inverse image and its agreement with the existing abelian functor; supplies the fixed-ring module comparison hypotheses.
Generic constant-ring and module inverse image for geometric morphisms, including composition and localization coherence; no finite coefficient assumption.
Generic base change of an etale covering used to retain each chosen trivializing cover.
Generic weakly-etale base change used for the arrows of pulled-back pro-etale trivializing covers.
Generic fpqc-cover base change, used with weakly-etale base change to retain pro-etale coverings.

Generic compatibility of module inverse image with restriction to localized sites, $(f_V)^*j_V^*\cong j_U^*f^*$; needed to pass from the pulled-back sheaf restricted to $T\times_SV_b$ to the localized pullback of the trivialized restriction on $V_b$. No node of the unit gives it.
